items.stem: Which one of the following pairs regarding Indian nationalism is correctly matched?

options.label: A
options.text: Sardar Patel : Hindustan Socialist Republican Army

options.label: B
options.text: Bhagat Singh : Swaraj Party

options.label: C
options.text: C.R. Das : Bardoli Satyagraha

options.label: D
options.text: Jawahar Lal Nehru : Oudh Kisan Sabha

items.answer: Sardar Patel led the Bardoli Satyagraha, Bhagat Singh belonged to the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army and C.R. Das founded the Swaraj Party with Motilal Nehru, so the first three pairs are wrong. Jawaharlal Nehru, along with Baba Ramchandra, helped set up the Oudh Kisan Sabha in October 1920. Hence the correctly matched pair is Jawahar Lal Nehru : Oudh Kisan Sabha.

items.stem: Which of the following was the reason for calling off 'the Non-cooperation Movement' by Gandhiji?

options.label: A
options.text: Pressure from the British Government

options.label: B
options.text: Second Round Table Conference

options.label: C
options.text: Gandhiji's arrest

options.label: D
options.text: Chauri-Chaura incident

items.answer: In February 1922 a crowd at Chauri-Chaura set fire to a police station and killed the policemen inside. Because the movement had turned violent and Gandhiji insisted that satyagraha must remain non-violent, he withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement. Hence the reason is the Chauri-Chaura incident.

Arrange the following events in the ascending year of their occurrence :-
1. Poona Act
2. Mahatma Gandhi got arrested
3. Gandhi Irwin Pact
4. Bhagat singh and two others were sentenced to death
items.answer: Mahatma Gandhi was arrested during the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930, the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in March 1931, Bhagat Singh and his two comrades were hanged in March 1931 after the pact, and the Poona Pact was signed in September 1932. In ascending order of occurrence the events are 2, 3, 4, 1.

items.stem:
Assertion : In 1917, Gandhiji organised a satyagraha to support the peasants of the Kheda district of Gujarat.
Reason : The peasants were affected by crop failure and plague epidemic. They could not pay the revenue and were demanding that revenue collection be relaxed.
items.assertion: In 1917, Gandhiji organised a satyagraha to support the peasants of the Kheda district of Gujarat.
items.reason: The peasants were affected by crop failure and plague epidemic. They could not pay the revenue and were demanding that revenue collection be relaxed.
items.answer: Gandhiji did organise a satyagraha in Kheda in 1917, so the assertion is true. The reason states exactly why he did so: crop failure and a plague epidemic had left the peasants unable to pay revenue and they wanted collection relaxed. The reason therefore correctly explains the assertion, so both are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

Arrange the following events in the correct sequence-
1. Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa.
2. Congress gave its support to Khilafat Movement.
3. Dandi March
4. Mahatma Gandhi travelled to champaran in Bihar to inspire the peasants to struggle against the oppressive plantation system.
items.answer: Gandhiji returned from South Africa in January 1915, went to Champaran in 1917, the Congress backed the Khilafat cause at the Calcutta session of 1920 and the Dandi March began in March 1930. The correct sequence is therefore 1, 4, 2, 3.

options.label: C
options.text: Britishers were not very much concerned about such movements.

options.label: D

items.answer: The photograph shows a very large gathering in which the front ranks are almost entirely women in white saris, standing in an organised procession before a public building. It records the entry of women in large numbers into nationalist processions during the Civil Disobedience Movement. Hence the picture shows that for the first time women joined nationalist processions in masses.

items.stem:
Assertion : Rich peasants became enthusiastic supporters of the Civil Disobedience Movement, organising their communities and at times forcing reluctant members to participate in the boycott programmes.
Reason : However, they were deeply happy when the movement was called off in 1931 with revenue rates being lowered.
items.assertion: Rich peasants became enthusiastic supporters of the Civil Disobedience Movement, organising their communities and at times forcing reluctant members to participate in the boycott programmes.
items.reason: However, they were deeply happy when the movement was called off in 1931 with revenue rates being lowered.
items.answer: Rich peasants such as the Patidars of Gujarat and the Jats of Uttar Pradesh did throw themselves into the Civil Disobedience Movement and pressed their communities to join the boycott, so the assertion is true. But when the movement was called off in 1931 without the revenue rates being revised, they were deeply disappointed, not happy. The reason is therefore false, so the assertion is true but the reason is false.

items.stem: Identify the appropriate reason for the formation of the Swaraj Party from the options given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Wanted members of Congress to return to Council Politics.

options.label: B
options.text: Wanted members of Congress to ask for Purna Swaraj for Indians.

options.label: C
options.text: Wanted members of Congress to ask Dominion State for India.

options.label: D
options.text: Wanted members of Congress to oppose Simon Commission.

items.answer: After the Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn, C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru argued that the Congress should re-enter the provincial councils and oppose British policy from within, and they formed the Swaraj Party for this purpose. Hence the Swaraj Party was formed because its leaders wanted members of Congress to return to Council Politics.

Assertion : Gandhiji entered into Gandhi-Irwin Pact on 5 March 1931.
Reason : Ghaffar Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru were both put in jail, the Congress was declared illegal, and a series of measures had been imposed to prevent meetings, demonstrations and boycotts.
items.assertion: Gandhiji entered into Gandhi-Irwin Pact on 5 March 1931.
items.reason: Ghaffar Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru were both put in jail, the Congress was declared illegal, and a series of measures had been imposed to prevent meetings, demonstrations and boycotts.
items.answer: Gandhiji did sign the Gandhi-Irwin Pact on 5 March 1931, so the assertion is true. It is also true that Ghaffar Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru were jailed, the Congress was declared illegal and repressive measures were imposed. These events describe the repression that preceded the pact rather than the reason Gandhiji signed it, so both statements are true but the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

items.stem:
Arrange the following in correct sequence:
1. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
2. Gandhi sent letter to Viceroy Lord Irwin.
3. Violation of Salt Act. by Mahatma Gandhi.
items.answer: Gandhiji first sent his letter of eleven demands to Viceroy Irwin on 31 January 1930, then broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930, and the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed only in March 1931. The correct sequence is therefore 2, 3, 1.

items.answer: The clues describe a method of struggle resting on the power of truth rather than physical force, in which the satyagrahi does not seek to destroy the opponent but to win him over. This is the idea of satyagraha that Gandhiji brought to the Indian national movement. Hence the agitation is Satyagraha.

• Some people come to attend the annual baisakhi fair
• The objective of such act was to "produce a moral effect"

items.answer: On 13 April 1919 a crowd gathered in the enclosed ground of Jallianwalla Bagh in Amritsar, some to protest against the repressive Rowlatt measures and some for the annual Baisakhi fair. General Dyer blocked the exit and ordered firing to, in his words, produce a moral effect. Hence the incident is the Jallianwalla Bagh Incident.

items.answer: The book gives the sequence as 4, 2, 3, 1, that is the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industries, the establishment of the Muslim League, the death of Lala Lajpat Rai and the launching of the Quit India Movement. Hence the answer is 4, 2, 3, 1.

Assertion : The council elections were boycotted in most provinces except Madras.
Reason : In many places, merchants and traders refused to trade in foreign goods or finance foreign trade.
items.assertion: The council elections were boycotted in most provinces except Madras.
items.reason: In many places, merchants and traders refused to trade in foreign goods or finance foreign trade.
items.answer: During the Non-Cooperation Movement the council elections were indeed boycotted in most provinces, Madras being the exception because the Justice Party saw the councils as a way for non-Brahmans to gain power. It is also true that merchants and traders refused to trade in or finance foreign goods. Both statements are true, but the traders' boycott of foreign goods does not explain why the councils were boycotted, so the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

Reason : The movement here was against Oudh Kisan Sabha.
items.assertion: In Awadh, the peasants were led by Alluri Sitaram Raju.
items.reason: The movement here was against Oudh Kisan Sabha.
items.answer: The peasants of Awadh were led by Baba Ramchandra, not by Alluri Sitaram Raju, who led the Gudem rebels of the Andhra hills, so the assertion is false. The Awadh movement was directed against talukdars and landlords, and the Oudh Kisan Sabha was in fact set up to organise the peasants, not opposed by them, so the reason is false as well. Hence both assertion and reason are false.

Assertion : The Non-Cooperation Movement gradually slowed down for a variety of reasons in the cities.
Reason : As the boycott movement spread, and people began discarding imported clothes and wearing only Indian ones, production of Indian textile mills and handlooms went up.
items.assertion: The Non-Cooperation Movement gradually slowed down for a variety of reasons in the cities.
items.reason: As the boycott movement spread, and people began discarding imported clothes and wearing only Indian ones, production of Indian textile mills and handlooms went up.
items.answer: The movement in the cities did slow down, because khadi was costly, Indian institutions were slow to come up and students and teachers drifted back to government schools, so the assertion is true. It is also true that the boycott of foreign cloth pushed up the output of Indian mills and handlooms. But that rise in Indian production was a success of the movement and does not explain why it slowed down, so both are true while the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

items.stem:
Arrange the following in the correct sequence: The Rowlatt Act:
1. Martial law was imposed, and General Dyer took command.
2. Gandhiji decided to launch a nationwide satyagraha against the proposed Rowlatt Act.
3. Local leaders were picked up from Amritsar, and Mahatma Gandhi was barred from entering Delhi.
4. It gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities.
items.answer: The book takes the story in the order 2, 4, 3, 1: Gandhiji decided on a nationwide satyagraha against the proposed Act, the Act gave the government enormous powers of repression, local leaders were then picked up from Amritsar and Gandhiji was barred from entering Delhi, and finally martial law was imposed with General Dyer in command. Hence the sequence is 2, 4, 3, 1.
items.ocr: Options (c) and (d) are printed identically as '4, 3, 2, 1'; the key is (a).

The famous image of Bharat Mata as a calm, composed, divine and ascetic figure was painted by Abanindranath Tagore, not Rabindranath Tagore, so the reason is certainly false, and the book treats the assertion as false too. Hence both assertion and reason are false.

items.stem:
This war was the first modern industrial war. It saw the use of machine guns, tanks, aircraft, chemical weapons, etc. on a massive scale. These were all increasingly products of modern large scale industry. To fight the war, millions of soldiers had to be recruited from around the world and moved to the frontlines on large ships and trains.
Analyse the above given information, considering one of the following correct option.

options.label: A
options.text: It is talking about the Industrial War

options.label: B
options.text: It is talking about the First World War

options.label: C
options.text: It is talking about the Cold War

options.label: D
options.text: It is talking about the Second World War

items.answer: The passage describes the first modern industrial war, fought with machine guns, tanks, aircraft and chemical weapons made by large scale industry, with millions of soldiers carried to the front by ship and train. This is the standard description of the First World War of 1914-18. Hence the passage is talking about the First World War.

items.stem:
Assertion : When Simon Commission arrived in India, it was greeted with the slogan 'Go back Simon'.
Reason : This happened as Mahatma Gandhi was on Dandi March during that time
items.assertion: When Simon Commission arrived in India, it was greeted with the slogan 'Go back Simon'.
items.reason: This happened as Mahatma Gandhi was on Dandi March during that time
items.answer: The Simon Commission did reach India in 1928 and was met everywhere with black flags and the cry 'Go back Simon', so the assertion is true. The protest was because the commission had no Indian member, and in any case the Dandi March took place only in 1930, two years later, so the reason is false. Hence the assertion is true but the reason is false.
